goldens.comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).

The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real issue in the catch block at lines 188-196. If the database update in the catch block fails (e.g., due to a missing row or database error), it will throw an exception that is not caught, which would abort the entire for loop processing remaining reminders. The catch block attempts to update retryCount but has no error handling for that update itself. This is a valid bug where a failure in the error-handling code path could cascade and prevent processing of subsequent reminders in the batch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: | P2 | packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:184 | Assigning the counter from the fetched value is non-atomic, so overlapping cron executions can overwrite each other's failures and bypass the retry cutoff. | correctness | 0.96 |

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a race condition. Looking at the diff, the code fetches `retryCount` from the database (line 56-57), then later uses `reminder.retryCount + 1` in updates (lines 184 and 193). If two cron executions run concurrently processing the same reminder, both could read the same retryCount value (e.g., 0), and both would write retryCount=1, effectively losing one failure count. This could allow more retries than intended before hitting the `gt: 1` deletion threshold. This is a real atomicity bug in the concurrent execution scenario.

adjudication_records.issue_text: | P1 | packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:38 | The retryCount OR branch is not constrained to SMS, so this SMS cleanup can delete EMAIL or WHATSAPP reminders with retryCount above one. | reliability | 0.99 |

adjudication.rationale: The finding is correct. Looking at the diff at lines 31-43, the deleteMany query uses an OR condition where the second branch only checks `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` without constraining it to `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`. This means any WorkflowReminder (EMAIL, WHATSAPP, etc.) with retryCount > 1 will be deleted by this SMS cleanup handler, which is clearly unintended behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: | P2 | packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:190 | If the retry-count update itself fails, the error escapes the per-reminder catch and aborts processing of every remaining reminder in the batch. | reliability | 0.94 |

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, the catch block at line 186-195 handles errors from the try block. Inside this catch block, there's a prisma.workflowReminder.update() call (lines 187-194) that is not wrapped in its own try-catch. If this database update fails, it will throw an exception that escapes the catch block. Since this is inside a loop processing reminders (the for loop iterating over unscheduledReminders), an unhandled exception would abort processing of all remaining reminders in the batch. This is a valid reliability concern - the error handling code itself can fail and cause broader failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: | P2 | packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:195 | Setting retryCount from the previously selected value loses increments when cron executions overlap, so failed reminders can exceed the intended retry limit. | reliability | 0.90 |

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real race condition. The code reads `reminder.retryCount` at query time (line 56-58), then later uses that cached value to increment (`reminder.retryCount + 1`) in the catch block around line 195. If two cron executions overlap, both could read retryCount=0, both fail, and both set retryCount=1 instead of one setting 1 and the other setting 2. This means reminders could exceed the retry limit of >1 (which triggers deletion). The diff shows this pattern clearly - the retryCount is selected once and used later without re-reading from the database.

adjudication_records.issue_text: | P1 | packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:39 | No test covers the unscoped retry cleanup, which can delete non-SMS reminders once retryCount exceeds one. | testing | 0.98 |

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a real bug in the diff. Looking at lines 31-43, the deleteMany query uses an OR condition where the second condition only checks `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` without any method filter. This means ANY WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1 will be deleted, regardless of whether it's SMS, EMAIL, or any other method. This is a logic error that could cause unintended deletion of non-SMS reminders. The finding is accurate about the unscoped nature of the retry cleanup condition.

adjudication_records.issue_text: | P2 | packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:178 | The new success, missing-result, thrown-error, and retry-limit branches have no behavioral tests, leaving the retry contract entirely unverified. | testing | 1.00 |

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new retry logic with multiple branches: (1) success case updating referenceId, (2) else branch incrementing retryCount when scheduledSMS is falsy, (3) catch block incrementing retryCount on errors, and (4) deletion of reminders with retryCount > 1. These are non-trivial behavioral changes that affect the retry contract. The finding correctly identifies that no test files are included in this diff to verify these new code paths. This is a legitimate testing gap for newly added business logic.
